newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Marvex buys Bulgaria's Devnya Cement for $44.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Marvex buys Bulgaria's Devnya Cement for $44.5 mln.

text.p: Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex signed an agreement with Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency on Wednesday to buy 70 percent of Devnya Cement for $44.5 million, the agency said.
"The treaty has been signed, the payment has been made and the shares have been endorsed," Privatisation Agency Executive Director Alexander Sabotinov told reporters.
The signing had to be postponed from Monday because of a delay in delivery of bank guarantees.

Marvex was set up for the privatisation deal and the Spanish side, led by Molturacion De Graneles, holds 80 percent. The remainder is held by Bulgarian private company Elva, which distributes Russian Lada cars in Bulgaria.
Molturacion is a private company established 1-1/2 years ago and owned by group of Spanish investors. It distributes cement and expects volume of 400,000 tonnes this year.
The company said it formed Marvex in an attempt to develop export markets for its cement. Marvex has pledged to invest $209.5 million in the Devnya plant over the next five years.
Rival bidder Ciments Francais said last week Marvex's business plan lacked credibility and asked the Bulgarian government to investigate. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188, 981 4145
